## New Investigation Idea

- **[2026-11-02] The 11-01 briefing proposes buying Build-A-Bear (BBW) at ~$27.61, citing Burry as corroboration. Eleven days earlier the paper book sold the same stock at $23.36 because it broke the 52-week low its thesis relied on. The Burry signal is also two months old.** The briefing card (fred-dashboard `morning-briefing.md`, 11-01) scores BBW 5/5 and calls it "the most-corroborated name on the screen", with `investor:burry` as one of its three signals. Two pages already in the wiki undercut that. First, [[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-10-12-BBW]] (Strategy F) entered at $25.58 on the same Burry thesis and left on 10-21 at $23.36 (−8.7%). It closed below the $24.22 52-week low that point 1 of its thesis leaned on, and [[finance/models/model-portfolio-management]] notes the thesis was never tested. The live card says nothing about this. The two books never see each other's exits. Second, BBW's row in [[finance/michael-burry/index]] still reads "20% down rule triggered … awaiting 10-Q" (08-29). The Part 1 write-up never got a Part 2, and none of the four Burry trading posts ingested after 09-09 (09-11 to 10-11) mentions BBW. So "Burry-held" is the same kind of unchecked label as the open 10-23 FLUT idea, this time on a new buy rather than an old holding. Before approving: (1) search Burry's Substack/X for any BBW post after 09-09 (a Part 2, an add or a sale) and ingest it; (2) read BBW's Q2 10-Q (filed ~early Sept), the one Burry was waiting for, for the impairment or inventory write-downs his thesis says were absent; (3) have the briefing's corroboration step also show the paper book's last verdict on any ticker it proposes. That way a name the paper book has just exited arrives with that history attached.

## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-11-01] S&P Global's Capital IQ review splits the company along the same line Work's Workday debate draws between weak and strong moats. Capital IQ sells analyst seats for data. Ratings sells a party who is accountable for the answer.** [[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-10-28-SPGI]] (open since 10-28) treats the possible Capital IQ separation as upside: a "purer, higher-multiple" ratings/indices group. Its key-risk point notes that the "AI disrupts financial data" narrative weighs on Market Intelligence, but it never asks why that narrative would hurt one half and not the other. [[work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026]] gives the test. LaRocque's strongest moat is compliance accountability ("someone must be held responsible"), which is exactly what a regulated credit rating is. The moats a16z thinks agents can erode (integration wiring, config skills, seat licences) are exactly what a data terminal is. Two pieces of the wiki back this up. Fred's own Phase 17 engine (built 10-31) already rebuilds the core Capital IQ task, fundamentals for US/UK/EU names from SEC XBRL and Yahoo, at no cost. And [[finance/ideas/idea-vistry-group]] found ~3x leverage that "Bloomberg/CapIQ/FactSet" standard data misses, so the value sits in the analyst, not the terminal. Read this way, the review is management admitting which half is exposed. If Capital IQ is sold or spun, the SPGI trade becomes a pure bet on the accountable half, and the spin-off itself becomes a natural short-research candidate (an AI-exposed seat business without its parent's buybacks). Caveat: SPGI gives no timetable, and Kensho/Visible Alpha could carry more proprietary data than this reading allows.
